ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy sha=28ed8395ff76 (2026-05-06T14:37:03Z) modified deploy/kafka/server.properties and inadvertently set offset.retention.minutes=1 (down from the correct value of 10080, i.e. 7 days). This change was applied to the replacement broker during a broker replacement procedure. With a 1-minute offset retention, all committed consumer group offsets for 'otel-pipeline-cg' expired within seconds of being written, causing the broker to continuously evict offset metadata. On every reconnect, the consumer found no stored offsets and reset to earliest (auto.offset.reset=earliest), forcing a full topic replay from offset 0. The resulting lag of 1.8M+ messages overwhelmed the otel-collector's heap and triggered a crash-restart loop that perpetuated the offset reset cycle.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately correct server.properties on the replacement broker: set offset.retention.minutes=10080 (7 days) to match the previous value documented in the config audit log. 2. Perform a rolling restart of kafka-broker-1 to apply the corrected configuration. 3. Once the broker is back up, manually reset the consumer group offsets for 'otel-pipeline-cg' to the latest committed high-watermark using: `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-broker-1:9092 --group otel-pipeline-cg --reset-offsets --to-latest --topic otel-spans --execute`. 4. Restart the otel-collector Kafka receiver to rejoin the consumer group from the correct offsets. 5. Add a config validation step to the broker-replacement-playbook.md and CI pipeline that asserts offset.retention.minutes >= 1440 before any broker is brought into production.
